children: WALL STREET EQUITY ALLOCATIONS REMAIN NEAR FOUR-YEAR HIGH, BOFA SAYS

An indicator tracking sell-side strategists' average recommended allocation to equities in a balanced fund remained in October at its highest level since March 2022,  leaving the closely watched contrarian sentiment gauge on the verge of flashing a sell signal, according to BofA Securities.

The Sell Side Indicator (SSI) was unchanged in October at 57.2%. The SSI is viewed as a contrarian gauge, with historically stronger future equity returns when strategists are bearish and weaker returns when they are heavily bullish.
The unchanged reading came despite significant shifts in the market. While the S&P 500
CBOE:SPX

slipped nearly 1% in October, the Russell 1000 Value Index (.RLV) outperformed its growth counterpart by 10 percentage points, the widest gap since 2001. The equal-weighted S&P 500 (.SPXEW) also beat the cap-weighted index by 6 percentage points, its largest advantage since 2009.

The SSI remains in neutral territory but is just 0.3 percentage points away from a sell signal, suggesting strategists remain broadly optimistic on stocks despite growing signs of investor exuberance, according to BofA analysts led by Victoria Roloff.

"With 3Q results from 60% of S&P 500 companies in, the EPS outlook remains strong: the ratio of above- to below-consensus EPS guides was 2.3x last month, well above the seasonal average," the analysts say.
(Chibuike Oguh)
